title: The Mirror Chamber Where Spirals Meet Themselves

features.name: the seagull in two directions
features.desc-on-touch: you see it facing east and west at once, as if the room itself is its own mirror; both are equally real

features.name: spiral that returns to itself
features.desc-on-touch: follow it inward and you emerge outward; the turn is so gradual you never notice the shape has inverted

features.name: the counting mirror
features.desc-on-touch: each spiral arm holds a notch; the mirror shows the same spiral but with twice as many notches; neither count is wrong

features.name: documentation of the mechanical bird
features.desc-on-touch: sketches and notes in archive hand, treating the seagull as zoological specimen; each page holds a different image of the same creature

features.name: the shell-hall
features.desc-on-touch: chambers within chambers; each shell shape contains another shell; the spiral teaches the room how to fold

inscription: here the mirror learned it was also a spiral, and the spiral learned it was also a mirror; they have not yet finished the conversation

file.name: Seagull_Zoological_Study_Contradictory.txt
file.note: field notes from two observers describing the same specimen; measurements differ; both observers equally reliable; archive: error in species definition or error in observation

exits.label: back to where floors still count themselves separately
toward chambers where reflection learns to see itself
into further mirrors, where the spiral grows a voice
